name: HCPC Standards of Conduct, Performance and Ethics
editionLabel: Revised standards in force from 1 September 2024
summary: The HCPC is the UK statutory regulator for 15 health and care professions, including practitioner psychologists such as clinical, counselling and health psychologists. Its standards of conduct, performance and ethics apply to every registrant and applicant, and the HCPC uses them when it considers fitness-to-practise concerns. The revised standards in force since 1 September 2024 strengthen expectations on equality, diversity and inclusion, speaking up about safety concerns, professional boundaries and social media. This is a summary in the app's own words. It is information, not legal advice.

keyReminders.text: Get valid consent before care, communicate in ways people understand, and support people with communication needs or limited English.
Keep information confidential and share it only when the law allows, there is consent, or it is needed to protect someone from serious harm.
Keep professional boundaries with service users and carers, including on social media and other online platforms.
Challenge discrimination, make reasonable adjustments, and do not let personal views affect the care you give.
Report and escalate concerns about the safety or wellbeing of service users, and be open when something goes wrong.

regulatorNote: The HCPC is itself the statutory regulator for practitioner psychologists in the UK. Counsellors and psychotherapists are usually on voluntary registers instead, such as BACP's.
